newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New FIRB chief doubts Australia big bank takeovers.
newsitem.headline: New FIRB chief doubts Australia big bank takeovers.

text.p: Australia's "big four" banks are unlikely to be taken over by foreign banks in the medium term, the recently appointed chairman of Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) said.

"There is no certainty, whatever is being said at the moment, that there will be bids for Australian banks, they are not easy for other banks to swallow, not the big ones," said FIRB's John Philips in a television interview.
Don Argus managing director of the country's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB), said 10 days ago that he felt his bank was vulnerable to foreign takeover.

Potential mergers and takeovers among Australia's four largest banks -- NAB, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, were ignited last month following the release of recommendations from an inquiry into the local financial system.
The inquiry, known as the Wallis inquiry, recommended mergers among the big four local banks and two largest insurance firms and said it did not object to foreign takeovers of local banks.
Philips told the Business Sunday programmes on Channel Nine television network that foreign takeovers of the four large banks are difficult.
"Not as easy as one might think when one reads some of the hyperbole that is being generated," Philips said.
Although Argus is opposed to foreign takeovers, he supports mergers amongst the domestic big four banks. NAB is seen as an acquirer if major domestic bank mergers were allowed to merge.
A takeover of NAB would cost almost A$30 billion, while a takeover of Westpac, ANZ or Commonwealth would cost around A$13 billion.
Foreign acquisitions of Australian companies have to be approved by FIRB.
